subject.title: fix(xai): gate server-side tools to xAI models only

question: Should xAI-billed server-side tools be exposed only when the active model provider is positively `xai`, or should OpenClaw preserve an explicit cross-provider opt-in path?
rationale: The patch fixes a credential-backed billing boundary, but it also changes existing default tool exposure when model metadata is missing or non-xAI, which is a maintainer-owned compatibility and security-boundary choice.

options.title: Accept fail-closed xAI-only exposure
options.body: Land this direction after adding factory tests, docs, and current-head proof that xAI runs keep the tools while non-xAI and missing-provider runs hide them.

options.title: Require explicit cross-provider opt-in
options.body: Pause this PR and design a visible opt-in or allowlist for users who intentionally want non-xAI models to call xAI-billed tools.

options.title: Keep credential-based exposure
options.body: Reject this PR and rely on documentation or warnings, accepting that configured xAI credentials can expose these billed tools to other providers.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed xAI-only exposure
recommendation.body: Land this direction after adding factory tests, docs, and current-head proof that xAI runs keep the tools while non-xAI and missing-provider runs hide them.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice spans plugin policy, active-model metadata, and compatibility rather than only the xAI implementation detail.
